pairs: who has taken away my judgment,
qui ad amaritudinem adduxit animam meam.
who has led my soul to bitterness,
Quia donec superest halitus in me,
as long as my breath remains in me
et spiritus Dei in naribus meis,
and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,
my lips will not speak iniquity,
nor will my tongue devise lies.
Absit a me ut justos vos esse judicem:
Far be it from me that I should judge you to be right,
I will not withdraw from my innocence.
I will not forsake my justification,
which I have just begun to grasp,
neque enim reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea.
for my heart does not find blame for me in my whole life.
Let the impious be as my enemy,
For what hope is there for the hypocrite,
et non liberet Deus animam ejus?
and God does not free his soul?
Will God pay attention to his cry,
Or will he take delight in the Almighty
and call upon God at all times?
Docebo vos per manum Dei quæ Omnipotens habeat,
I will teach you through the hand of God, what the Almighty holds,
and I will not conceal it.
et quid sine causa vana loquimini?
and so why do you speak vain things without a reason?
Hæc est pars hominis impii apud Deum,
This is the portion of the impious man with God,
and the inheritance of the violent,
which they will receive from the Almighty.
If his sons should happen to increase,
they will be for the sword,
et nepotes ejus non saturabuntur pane:
and his grandsons will not be satisfied with bread.
qui reliqui fuerint ex eo sepelientur in interitu,
Whatever will remain of him will be buried in the ruins,
and his widows will not weep.
If he will amass silver as if it were dirt
and fabricate garments as if they were clay,
but the just will be clothed with it and the innocent will divide the silver.
He has built his house like a moth,
and he has made a makeshift shelter like a sentry.
the rich man will leave him with nothing;
aperiet oculos suos, et nihil inveniet.
he will open his eyes and find nothing.
Destitution will surround him like water;
a storm will overwhelm him in the night.
Tollet eum ventus urens, et auferet,
A burning wind will pick him up and carry him away,
et velut turbo rapiet eum de loco suo.
and, like a whirlwind, it will rush him from his place.
And it will hurl over him and will not spare him;
He will clasp his hands over himself,
and he will hiss at himself,
